newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bullish Norwegian shares hit another life high.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Norwegian shares hit another life high.

text.p: Norwegian shares, led by blue chips, rallied to another peak on Monday and may test the psychological 1,000-point mark if Wall Street continues to perform well.
The Oslo Bourse Total index climbed 1.42 percent to 992.42 points, its 57th record closing high in little more than a year. Trade was heavy at 1.1 billion crowns.

Dealers said the index was influenced by U.S. developments and Norway's strong economy. Gains were registered across the board with industrial and banking shares doing best, including Norsk Hydro and Den norske Bank (DnB).
"There is very good liquidity," one dealer said.
"If Wall Street performs well tonight we will break through the 1,000-point mark tomorrow," he predicted.
Norsk Hydro, Norway's biggest company, rose 1.44 percent to 353 crowns and was the most traded share at 131 million crowns.
"Hydro is doing fine thanks to the high oil prices and many investors feel Hydro is one of the best buys now. The focus is on blue chips because they are deemed to be safe bets."
DnB, Norway's top bank, closed 3.19 percent higher at 25.90 crowns. Metals maker Elkem climbed 2.25 percent to 113.50 crowns on expectations of rising ferrochrome prices, a dealer said.
